title: Two Voices Trading Short Lines
tests: Tests distinct speaker assignment and ordered dialogue in one audio-only output, and recognition that standalone speech synthesis is outside the listed free-tier tools.

exact_text.text: Almost. Have you got the tickets?
exact_text.read_as: Almost. Have you got the tickets?

faults.what: The supplied transcription contains only B's second line; the first, third, and fourth lines are missing, leaving the requested exchange incomplete.

judge.summary: The eight-second audio contains only one of the four requested lines rather than the complete two-voice conversation.

must_haves.item: All four lines are spoken exactly as supplied, in the supplied order, without reading the labels.
must_haves.why: Only “Almost. Have you got the tickets?” appears in the supplied speech transcription.

must_haves.item: Two clearly distinguishable voices are audible, with A lower and B higher.
must_haves.why: The transcription provides no audible voice characteristics, and only one line is reported.

must_haves.item: Each voice consistently reads its assigned lines: A first and third, B second and fourth.
must_haves.why: The first, third, and fourth lines are absent, so the required voice assignments are not completed.

must_haves.item: The conversation sounds friendly and natural, lasts approximately 8 seconds, and has no overlapping or cut-off lines.
must_haves.why: The reported duration is eight seconds, but friendliness, naturalness, overlap, and cutoff cannot be assessed from the transcription alone.

must_haves.item: One standalone audio file contains the complete exchange, with no music or sound effects.
must_haves.why: One audio file, dialogue.wav, is reported, but it does not contain the complete exchange. The absence of music or sound effects cannot be verified from the supplied transcription.
